message.content: The common ancestor of lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) is a member of the order **Carnivora** that lived during the Miocene epoch, roughly 20–25 million years ago. This ancestor was part of the early **Feliformia** lineage that gave rise to modern cats, and it shared traits with the early **Caniformia** lineage that eventually led to equids (horses, zebras, donkeys). In other words, lions and zebras diverged from a shared Miocene ancestor that was a small, carnivorous mammal within the broader clade of early carnivorans.
